displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The strongest religious-pragmatist case treats God-language as a disciplined name for an experientially encountered, culturally accumulated, and action-organizing reality, while making only a modest metaphysical claim that this convergence deserves serious evidential consideration.

novelty.explanation: This repairs unstable movement among functional and ontological senses by stating a limited convergence claim rather than asserting their identity.

premises.text: Religious narratives can encode practical and moral understanding in forms that are not scientific theories yet still guide perception, judgment, and action across generations.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's distinction between scientific status and embodied narrative understanding.

premises.text: Mystical experiences merit investigation because their durable psychological consequences show that they are not merely momentary verbal beliefs, although durability alone does not establish supernatural causation.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the empirical significance of lasting effects while correcting the unsupported transition from efficacy to external correspondence.

premises.text: Every moral framework begins from value-laden commitments, so secular frameworks should disclose and defend their starting values rather than presenting them as normatively neutral facts.

novelty.explanation: This extends the foundational challenge while avoiding any inference that contestability itself establishes a religious foundation.

premises.text: Highest values, inherited narratives, and communal rituals can jointly organize attention and conduct in ways that exceed any isolated proposition or finite list of explicit rules.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the rule-system argument by emphasizing distributed practical organization without inferring a metaphysical substrate from computation alone.

premises.text: Naturalistic explanations of religious cognition and cultural attribution can be accepted as causal contributors without thereby settling every question about the total reality interpreted through religious experience.

novelty.explanation: This replaces exclusivist causal competition with a layered account compatible with acknowledged natural mechanisms and continued metaphysical inquiry.

conclusion.text: Therefore, God-language may reasonably be retained as a fallible interpretive framework for ultimate value, transformative experience, and inherited practical wisdom, while any stronger claim about a supernatural agent remains separately evidentially accountable.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately preserves the religious framework while expressly separating it from an unsupported supernatural-agent inference.

newArguments.title: Convergent practical realism
newArguments.text: When independent religious practices repeatedly coordinate attention, sacrifice, communal trust, confrontation with mortality, and long-term character formation, their convergence may constitute evidence for a real domain of human life even if no single doctrine literally describes a supernatural object. The relevant realism is modest: it claims that the organized pattern is discoverable rather than arbitrarily invented. Competing traditions and naturalistic explanations remain relevant tests, but functional convergence gives investigators a reason to examine religious categories as possible maps of recurring experiential and social structure.

novelty.explanation: This newly argues from cross-practice convergence to a modest realism about a domain of life, without attributing supernatural agency.

newArguments.title: Transmission-cost asymmetry
newArguments.text: A secular culture may preserve individual moral propositions while losing the narrative, ritual, and communal systems that make those propositions memorable, motivationally salient, and resilient under crisis. That possibility can be tested by comparing transmission costs, behavioral durability, and intergenerational retention across religious and nonreligious institutions. The argument does not assume religion is uniquely successful; it identifies an empirical burden often missed when inheritance is treated as detachable information. If religious forms reliably lower those transmission costs, retaining or adapting them could be rational even under metaphysical uncertainty.

novelty.explanation: This develops the inheritance route into a testable institutional claim about transmission rather than assuming religious indispensability.

thesis.text: The strongest secular-skeptical case grants the psychological, moral, and cultural achievements of religion while insisting that each supernatural claim remain independently testable and that human institutions preserve useful inheritance through transparent, revisable methods.

novelty.explanation: This integrates the transcript's evidential distinction, inheritance concession, and positive secular orientation into one proportionate thesis.

premises.text: A belief's usefulness, emotional depth, cultural longevity, or transformative effect can make it important without logically demonstrating the existence of the entity named in its traditional interpretation.

novelty.explanation: This generalizes the central truth-utility distinction across the principal kinds of significance discussed.

premises.text: Cultural learning, pattern recognition, and agency detection provide independently plausible pathways from intense experience to supernatural attribution, so external agency requires discriminating evidence beyond phenomenological intensity.

novelty.explanation: This combines the transcript's naturalistic mechanisms and specifies the additional evidence required for external attribution.

premises.text: Acknowledging unresolved consciousness is epistemically responsible when available explanations remain incomplete, and such acknowledgment does not prevent inquiry into either material or metaphysical possibilities.

novelty.explanation: This preserves restraint while clarifying that uncertainty permits investigation without licensing an unsupported conclusion.

premises.text: Moral systems can make objective comparisons relative to disclosed goals, revise foundations when evidence exposes conflict, and retain responsibility through reflective agency without libertarian freedom.

novelty.explanation: This unifies the transcript's error correction, adaptive learning, and compatibilist agency into a stronger secular moral model.

premises.text: Useful religious knowledge can be preserved, criticized, and retransmitted by institutions that openly separate historical provenance from supernatural endorsement and measure whether preservation actually succeeds.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the underdeveloped feasibility question by adding institutional transparency and empirical evaluation of preservation.

conclusion.text: Therefore, society may retain religious metaphors, practices, and inherited wisdom where they prove beneficial while withholding belief in supernatural agents until distinct evidence supports those ontological claims.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion preserves useful religious material while maintaining the transcript's separate evidential burden for supernatural agency.

newArguments.title: Interpretive portability test
newArguments.text: If a religious practice produces moral or psychological benefits, researchers can translate its active components into alternative narratives and compare outcomes across believers, nonbelievers, and members of different traditions. Benefits that survive translation support the view that the mechanism is humanly portable rather than dependent on one supernatural interpretation. Benefits that disappear would identify a genuine explanatory challenge for secular substitutes. This test respects religious experience while converting claims of indispensability into comparative evidence about ritual, community, expectation, identity, and narrative framing.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an empirical translation test for distinguishing portable human mechanisms from interpretation-specific dependence.

newArguments.title: Institutional error-correction advantage
newArguments.text: Separating supernatural authority from inherited moral wisdom can improve correction when traditions contain both valuable guidance and harmful historical residues. A secular institution can document provenance, retain practices that demonstrate benefit, publish reasons for revision, and permit affected communities to challenge outcomes without treating any text as beyond reconsideration. Religious institutions can adopt similar procedures, but their success would then depend on transparent human evaluation rather than asserted supernatural authorization. This creates a practical reason to distinguish cultural inheritance from ontology even when both remain present in the same community.

novelty.explanation: This extends revision and inheritance into an institutional argument about transparent correction and accountable preservation.
